scenario_description:
Objective: Prevent tonight's hard freeze from threatening private-well pressure controls through an open crawlspace vent.
Emerging Need: A short afternoon absence, a severe low-temperature forecast, an observed open vent, and then an extended station commitment progressively make pre-evening protection time-sensitive.
Decision Context: Stored well-winter notes identify the symptom combination, safe non-invasive scope, exact pressure-switch check, and routine service route.
Consequence: After the routine route closes, no freezing or water loss has occurred, but the cabin lacks the intended preventive check before the coldest hours. Routine dispatch closes before the forecast freeze. A private vent-closure reminder remains useful while Seren can act personally; the extended shift makes the approved service route relevant.

parameter.body: Tonight's forecast low has been revised to -14 F between 20:00 and 23:00, with northwest wind. Exposed crawlspace plumbing and well-pressure controls may need pre-evening protection.

parameter.content: Walking past your drive after checking plow stakes: the north crawlspace vent cover looks propped open a few inches. No water or ice visible. I'm leaving for Burlington at noon.
